title: Legal Research and Case Strategy
answer: Retrieval-grounded research, adversarial statutory reading, brief drafting, citation auditing and jurisdictional anomalies.

children.name: Retrieval-Grounded Legal Research
children.blurb: Retrieval-grounded legal research is a method that anchors every answer, summary, or draft to specific passages from primary and secondary legal sources, such as case law, statutes, regulations, and court filings.

children.name: Adversarial Statutory Interpretation
children.blurb: Adversarial statutory interpretation is the use of AI to identify competing readings of a statute, model how a court or regulator might resolve ambiguity, and surface arguments that favor one side in litigation or compliance disputes.

children.name: Brief Drafting with Machine Assistance
children.blurb: Brief drafting with machine assistance covers using language models and legal research tools to produce, revise, and check written submissions such as motions, memoranda, and appellate briefs.

children.name: Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking
children.blurb: Citation auditing and good law checking is the process of verifying that every authority cited in a legal document remains valid, has not been overruled or negatively treated, and still supports the proposition for which it is cited.

children.name: Jurisdictional Anomalies and Local Codes
children.blurb: Jurisdictional anomalies and local codes in AI law cover situations where state, municipal, or sector-specific rules diverge from federal or general principles, creating uneven obligations for developers and users.

sections.body: Legal research and case strategy now uses artificial intelligence to search case law, statutes, and regulations, retrieve passages, and draft summaries or argument sections. Retrieval-grounded systems anchor their output to specific documents rather than generating from memory alone. Adversarial statutory reading tools are used to test a proposed interpretation against counterarguments and alternative readings. Brief drafting assistance produces first drafts of motions, memos, and other filings from a set of facts and authorities. Citation auditing checks whether cited cases still stand and whether quotes match the source. Jurisdictional anomaly tools flag local rules, court-specific requirements, and unusual code provisions that a general model might miss.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven, with retrieval of exact text and basic citation format checking largely solved when the system has access to a current database. Adversarial statutory interpretation remains a human task, with machine assistance limited to surfacing possible counter-readings and relevant canons. Brief drafting can produce usable first drafts, but every generated sentence must be checked for accuracy and tone. Citation auditing tools catch many formatting errors and flag overturned cases, yet they still miss substantive weaknesses and sometimes fail to recognize when a case has been implicitly limited. Jurisdictional anomalies are the least solved area, because local codes and court practices change frequently and are often not digitized in a consistent way. The site tracks 142 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which shows how quickly the underlying law shifts and how easily a static model can fall behind.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would start with Retrieval-Grounded Legal Research to see how systems anchor answers to actual case text and statutes instead of relying on model memory. Adversarial Statutory Interpretation then shows how the same tools are used to stress-test a reading against opposing arguments and canons of construction. Brief Drafting with Machine Assistance covers the generation of argument sections, fact statements, and memos, and explains what parts still need a lawyer's judgment. Citation Auditing and Good Law Checking is where a reader would go to understand how tools verify that cited cases remain good law and that quotations are accurate. Jurisdictional Anomalies and Local Codes addresses the patchwork of state and local rules, including the 6,823 state AI bills this site tracks, and why a general model often misses court-specific requirements.
